topics.title: Travaux de cours
topics.summary: Appropriate personal study and formative use is broadly permitted subject to local rules. In summative assessment, presenting unacknowledged AI-generated content as your own is misconduct unless the assessment brief explicitly states otherwise. Engineering and Manufacturing Engineering Triposes have additional conditions.
topics.scope: Read the school, course, assessment and audience scope in each quoted claim

claims.text: A student using any unacknowledged content generated by artificial intelligence within a summative assessment as though it is their own work constitutes academic misconduct, unless explicitly stated otherwise in the assessment brief.

evidence.quote: “A student using any unacknowledged content generated by artificial intelligence within a summative assessment as though it is their own work constitutes academic misconduct, unless explicitly stated otherwise in the assessment brief.” Plagiarism & Academic Misconduct

evidence.location: Derived source text lines 119-119; exact character range 2777:3045; original source representation retained

claims.text: Cambridge broadly permits appropriate GenAI use for personal study, research and formative work, with nuanced Department, Faculty or College guidance controlling the context. Students should check local rules with staff; this is not blanket permission for summative assessments.

evidence.quote: The University of Cambridge broadly permits the appropriate use of GenAI tools and related software, however, due to the variety of disciplines and research areas present at the institution, there is need for more nuanced guidance at local levels.
evidence.title: Generative AI and Education | Blended Learning Service
evidence.location: Derived source text lines 133-133; exact character range 6450:6697; original source representation retained

evidence.quote: Students are permitted to make appropriate use of GenAI tools to support their personal study, research and formative work. Appropriate use is better defined locally by Department, Faculty, or College depending on the context and you should always check with a member of staff to be sure you know how you are able to use these tools for your education. General guidance for use of GenAI is available as well as specific guidance for assessment-related queries.
evidence.title: Generative AI and Education | Blended Learning Service
evidence.location: Derived source text lines 135-135; exact character range 6941:7401; original source representation retained

claims.text: The Engineering and Manufacturing Engineering Triposes’ policy, approved by the Faculty Board in June 2026, requires declaring all GenAI used to prepare summative work unless the assessment brief states otherwise. Assignment-specific rules take precedence. Students must not generate raw submission/presentation content without an initial self-written base or automatically generate references from content; tools managing student-identified references remain allowed. Students are responsible for submitted work and are expected to explain it; marks reflect unmet learning outcomes even when no academic misconduct is established.

topics.title: Confidentialité et données sensibles
topics.summary: Educational and research data rules apply in their own contexts. Staff administrative guidance explicitly excludes student learning, assessment and research. Examiners may not upload student work to GenAI.
topics.scope: Read the school, course, assessment and audience scope in each quoted claim

claims.text: Cambridge says examiners across undergraduate, taught-postgraduate and research-postgraduate programmes may not upload, copy or share student work with GenAI/LLMs or use them to analyse submissions and produce feedback. The source also prohibits sharing student IP/submissions without student permission because of uncertain storage/use. Examiners may use AI to support their own feedback writing, such as consolidating personal notes or rephrasing comments; this is not blanket permission to upload student work.

evidence.quote: Examiners across all programmes of study (including Undergraduate, Postgraduate Taught, and Postgraduate Research) are not permitted to upload, copy, or share student work with Generative AI (GenAI) tools and Large Language Models (LLMs).
evidence.title: Generative AI and Assessment | Blended Learning Service
evidence.location: Derived source text lines 130-130; exact character range 5103:5341; original source representation retained

evidence.quote: Examiners may not use tools, such as ChatGPT, Perplexity, Google Bard, or Microsoft Copilot, to analyse work submitted by students and provide written feedback.
evidence.title: Generative AI and Assessment | Blended Learning Service
evidence.location: Derived source text lines 130-130; exact character range 5342:5502; original source representation retained

evidence.quote: Due to lack of clarity and uncertainty of how these tools use and/or store input data, it is not permitted to share student IP and submitted work without permission from the student.
evidence.title: Generative AI and Assessment | Blended Learning Service
evidence.location: Derived source text lines 130-130; exact character range 5503:5685; original source representation retained

evidence.quote: Where preferred, however, examiners may use these tools to support their own writing in the process of documenting feedback (e.g., consolidating personal notes and rephrasing comments).
evidence.title: Generative AI and Assessment | Blended Learning Service
evidence.location: Derived source text lines 131-131; exact character range 5686:5871; original source representation retained

claims.text: Cambridge’s staff administrative-use guidance recommends avoiding confidential, sensitive or personal data in GenAI unless warranted and consistent with the guidance. This document expressly excludes teaching, student learning/assessment, research, and College or other separate-entity business. It is not an unconditional privacy prohibition for all student AI use.

evidence.quote: Regardless of the work being undertaken, it is recommended that staff avoid inputting confidential, sensitive or personal information into GenAI tools unless warranted and only in accordance with this guidance.

claims.text: Version 4 of Cambridge’s Research Data Management Policy Framework, reviewed on 25 June 2026, requires its research community, including staff and students involved in research, to comply with applicable University, funder and publisher requirements for GenAI in research, dissemination, funding applications and research assessment. Relevant issues include sensitive data, ownership, copyright, ethics, integrity and security. The framework says there is no distinct University GenAI research policy; that does not mean research has no AI-related rules.

evidence.quote: Complying with any requirements from the University, research funders, or publishers when using Generative AI as a tool when undertaking or disseminating research, or when applying for funding, or in the assessment of research.
evidence.title: Research Data Management Policy Framework | Open Research
evidence.location: Derived source text lines 187-187; exact character range 17736:17963; original source representation retained

evidence.quote: The use of Generative AI tools has implications for sensitive data (e.g. personal, confidential), data ownership, copyright, intellectual property, research ethics and integrity, information security, and environmental sustainability, including when reusing research data created utilising them.
evidence.title: Research Data Management Policy Framework | Open Research
evidence.location: Derived source text lines 187-187; exact character range 17964:18259; original source representation retained

evidence.quote: At present there is no distinct University policy for using Generative AI tools in research.

evidence.quote: This policy framework applies to all members of staff and students and research-enabling staff (e.g. professional services, technical) at the University.

claims.text: Cambridge says examiners across undergraduate, taught-postgraduate and research-postgraduate programmes may not upload, copy or share student work with GenAI/LLMs or use them to analyse submissions and produce feedback.
